external.name: pi-lens
external.review: MIT; Node >=22.19.0. Static review of the supplied 4.4.4 package only; no package code executed or TUI/model-provider validation. Native @ast-grep/napi ^0.50.0, @ast-grep/cli 0.50.0 (dependency lifecycle platform binary setup), bundled core/vendor tree-sitter WASM and optional web-tree-sitter 0.25.10; no runtime typescript dependency. No preinstall/install/postinstall in this manifest; prepare is a source-build hook (build, grammar download, git hooks, lock stamping, loader warming), not a registry-install hook. Registers 13 pi tools: adds symbol_search, project_report, effective_config, lens_diagnostic_mark and pi_lens_activate_tools; removes ast_grep_dump, ast_dump and standalone lsp_diagnostics. Exact firewall entries allow analysis/config/discovery, ask for structural replacement, LSP navigation and diagnostic suppression; path checks include paths arrays and analysisRoot (tests/tool-firewall-smoke.ts, tests/firewall-shell-smoke.ts). Diagnostics also run in process through session/write/edit/turn hooks, outside tool-call isolation. Profiles select the companion as a whole; balanced does not filter its registered tools. The earlier dependency warning applies to 3.8.63: 4.4.4 declares optional peers pi-coding-agent=* and pi-tui=*, typebox=^1.0.0. pi 1.3 warns on host packages in dependencies, not this manifest, though typebox still differs from the recommended wildcard. The kit defaults PI_LENS_DISABLE_LSP_INSTALL=1 and PI_LENS_DISABLE_TOOL_INSTALL=1; 4.4.4 honours both, including managed refreshes. Existing tools keep working. Missing non-vendored grammar downloads are separately trust-gated and not disabled by these switches; hash checking depends on a matching grammars.lock.json entry. See docs/supply-chain.md for the registration diff and limits.

external.name: pi-lean-ctx
external.review: Apache-2.0. OPT-IN, in no profile: it needs the external `lean-ctx` Rust CLI (`cargo install lean-ctx` or brew; not bundled, not in this package's supply chain) and, in its default additive mode, registers extra model-visible tools even when that CLI is absent (ctx_shell, ctx_read, ctx_ls, ctx_find, ctx_grep, lean_ctx, ctx_edit; checked against 3.10.5 in a real pi 0.85.1 TUI). Those tools are not inspected the way the built-in ones are: secret-guard matches the built-in names bash/write/edit, so ctx_shell and ctx_edit are outside its checks, and tool-firewall sees them only as unknown tools (policy default: ask) rather than as shell commands. Enable it only for trusted repositories and expect an approval prompt per call; it is installed by `install.ts --all` only when its binary is on PATH. Installing 3.10.5 (verified to load and degrade gracefully without the CLI) replaces 3.8.18, whose review here wrongly said it adds no visible tools.

external.name: pi-readseek
external.review: MIT. @jarkkojs/readseek (native) + xxhash-wasm. Hash-anchored read/edit/grep + structural code maps + AST search — a lean file-I/O primitive for navigating large repos cheaply. Registers replacement tools (manual). 0.10.1 was evaluated and not adopted: its licence is now Apache-2.0 (this review covers the MIT 0.4.x line), the entry moved to dist/index.ts and it depends on @jarkkojs/readseek-api; 0.4.26 stays pinned until 0.10.x has been reviewed as a whole.
